questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Gabon?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Gabon article.

questions.proof: Its capital is Libreville, which is also the largest city in the country.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Gabon?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Gabon on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Gabon article.

questions.proof: That was a state that included parts of what is today Angola and Republic of Congo.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Gabon?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Gabon article.

questions.proof: In the 19th century, the French made Gabon part of their Colonial empire.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It has borders with Equatorial _____, Cameroon, and the Republic of the Congo.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Equatorial”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Gabon article.

questions.proof: It has borders with Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon, and the Republic of the Congo.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Under his governance Gabon had just one political party between _____ and 1990.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Politics” part of the Gabon article.

questions.proof: Under his governance Gabon had just one political party between 1968 and 1990.
